messages:
maria: FYI master CI turned red on linux-64, intermittent failure in TestKVSync. failing ~1/30 runs.

maria: snippet from the job: 
```
--- FAIL: TestKVSync (0.12s)
    kv_sync_test.go:87: expected 3 entries, got 2
    kv_sync_test.go:102: timed out waiting for write acknowledgement
FAIL
```

ci-bot: Build #4621 failed on linux-x86_64 (link: https://ci.internal/r/4621) :x:

aj: @maria can you /rerun? if it's flaky maybe a quick rerun will green it.

maria: rerun requested, ci-bot queued it. also adding seed info from the job logs: `SEED=9273412`.

devon: saw this pop up yesterday on my branch too. symptoms look like the write ack goroutine sometimes gets preempted and the test times out. not sure if it's scheduler jitter or a real ordering bug.

naveen: can we reproduce locally with the same seed? try: `go test ./runtime -run TestKVSync -seed 9273412 -v`

maria: ran locally with that seed, reproduces ~10% of attempts. with `-race` it failed immediately for me. output shows a small window where a token update is dropped.

eva: interesting. the test relies on a background retry ticker at 50ms. if the test runner gets delayed the ack coming after a retry could be processed in the wrong window. maybe increase the timeout in test or tighten synchronization.

aj: i'd prefer we avoid just increasing timeouts. can we add a deterministic hook to the test to avoid timing-dependence? e.g., expose a `FlushPending()` helper in the kv test harness and wait for it.

devon: agree. short-term: marking the test flaky in CI to avoid blocking merges while we fix. long-term: add explicit synchronization and remove ticker reliance.

maria: created a quick PR to mark it flaky: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 (WIP). requesting reviewers @aj @devon.

naveen: for bisecting, we should run the failing test under heavy CPU starvation to try to stress the window. command I used: `taskset -c 1 go test ./runtime -run TestKVSync -seed 9273412` and `stress-ng --cpu 3 --timeout 10s` in parallel. that made it reproduce reliably.

aj: good repro. can someone try instrumenting the code path and log the timeline around the ack and the retry? even a couple `log.Printf` lines will help.

devon: I put a small instrument patch on my fork and pushed logs to the CI run: https://ci.internal/r/4622/logs. looks like the ack goroutine isn't acquiring the same mutex in rare cases because we early-return on `ctx.Done()` in one path.

maria: that sounds promising — maybe when the test cancels context during teardown the ack handler exits before processing an in-flight callback. adding a nil-check/atomic flag might avoid the race.

eva: can we add a fix that ensures in-flight callbacks are drained before ctx cancellation? that would make the runtime more robust rather than changing tests.

aj: plan: (1) mark flaky in CI to unbreak master (maria PR), (2) add deterministic drain helper and change test to use it (devon + naveen), (3) add defensive fix in ack handling so cancellation doesn't lose callbacks (devon), (4) unmark flaky once green.

maria: PR for flaky marker merged, CI green on rerun for now. opening follow-up issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412 (drain helper), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/413 (ack-defensive-fix).

naveen: I'll grab the drain helper change, push a small test that uses it and run the stress repro overnight.

devon: I'll work the defensive fix. will request review from @aj and @maria once ready.

aj: thanks all. if anyone sees the failure in other branches ping this thread.

maria: thanks folks — leaving links to logs and reproducer in the issues. :thumbsup:
